newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs stable and quiet, demand light.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs stable and quiet, demand light.

text.p: Spot U.S. liquefied petroleum gas prices were stable in quiet late afternoon trade on Monday, players said, as oil markets took a breather from last week's sinking.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane remained between 34.75 cents and 35.00 cents a gallon in a market lacking in news.
Traders said small parcels of prompt deals were done at 35.25 cents.
In the Midwest, where frigid weather activated some buying this morning, spot propane was seen as quiet except for some short covering by traders.
"There is not much concern about the weather," said a Conway trader, noting good stock levels in tertiary storage.
The butane markets were also quiet now that blending season has ended.
Belvieu normal butane traded at 39.25 cents and Conway material sold for 33.25 cents and 33.50 cents.
Meanwhile, world oil prices stayed largely stable after plunging nearly nine percent last week to nine month lows.
